title: Book 11 · Only men suffers inflection in the plural possessive: the Inglis

verses.t: menis fewte_ (VIII. 19), of othir mennis landis (XI. 148). In till Scottis men possessioune (XVII. 202) we may have, as Henschel suggests, a piece of “scribal carelessness;” but Hampole undoubtedly uses this as a valid form:

“Sal dede men banes be set togyder
Thurgh messes, and rightwis men prayers.”
Murray, Dialect of the Southern Counties, p. 153.
Darstellung der Flexionslehre in John Barbour’s Bruce, p. 12.
